paragraphs.text: «أَرْبَعٌ مَنْ كُنَّ فِيهِ كَانَ مُنَافِقًا خَالِصًا، وَمَنْ كَانَتْ فِيهِ خَلَّةٌ مِنْهُنَّ كَانَتْ فِيهِ خَلَّةٌ مِنْ نِفَاقٍ حَتَّى يَدَعَهَا: إِذَا حَدَّثَ كَذَبَ، وَإِذَا عَاهَدَ غَدَرَ، وَإِذَا وَعَدَ أَخْلَفَ، وَإِذَا خَاصَمَ فَجَرَ».

en.text: Hadith Established source translation

“There are four (traits); whoever has them is a sheer hypocrite, and whoever has one trait of them has one of the traits of hypocrisy until he gives it up: whenever he speaks, he tells a lie; whenever he makes a covenant, he proves treacherous; whenever he makes a promise, he breaks it; and whenever he is in a dispute, he behaves in a shameless immoral manner."
Source: Abdullah ibn Amr. Sahih Muslim 58; jointly reported. Arabic and established translations: HadeethEnc, record 65124. Numbering follows that record.
Status: Sahih according to the source classification.
Relevance: The source explanation distinguishes practical hypocrisy from automatically declaring a person outside Islam.

paragraphs.text: «إِذَا الْتَقَى الْمُسْلِمَانِ بِسَيْفَيْهِمَا فَالْقَاتِلُ وَالْمَقْتُولُ فِي النَّارِ»، فَقُلْتُ: يَا رَسُولَ اللهِ هَذَا الْقَاتِلُ، فَمَا بَالُ الْمَقْتُولِ؟ قَالَ: «إِنَّهُ كَانَ حَرِيصًا عَلَى قَتْلِ صَاحِبِهِ».

en.text: Hadith Established source translation

"When two Muslims meet to fight each other with their swords, both the killer and the killed are doomed to Hellfire." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, that is the case with the killer, but what about the killed one?" He said: "Indeed, he was keen to kill his companion."
Source: Abu Bakrah. Sahih al-Bukhari 31; jointly reported. Arabic and established translations: HadeethEnc, record 4304. Numbering follows that record.
Status: Sahih according to the source classification.
Relevance: The explanation expressly concerns intention to kill; it must not be used to equate innocent victims with aggressors.
Best use: Evidence / ethical principle

en.text: Hadith Established source translation

"Support your brother whether he is an oppressor or oppressed." A man said: O Messenger of Allah, I support him if he is oppressed, but how should I support him if he is an oppressor? He said: "Stop—or prevent—him from oppression. This is indeed supporting him."
Source: Anas ibn Malik. Sahih al-Bukhari 6952; numbering displayed by HadeethEnc. Arabic and established translations: HadeethEnc, record 4236. Numbering follows that record.
Status: Sahih according to the source classification.
Relevance: Redefines support for one’s own group as preventing its wrongdoing, not excusing it.
